text: Core positioning: The research focuses on enterprises (including for-profit organizations and some non-profit organizations), concentrating on management issues throughout their entire lifecycle, covering both practical aspects such as "how to improve efficiency and reduce costs" and top-level design issues such as "how to formulate strategies and stimulate organizational vitality," ultimately achieving the optimal allocation of resources such as "people, finance, materials, and information." Research scope: Functional dimension: Covers the core functions of enterprise management, including strategic management, marketing, human resource management, financial management, operation management, organizational behavior, etc. Organizational dimension: Involves the management characteristics of different types of enterprises (such as small and medium-sized enterprises, multinational companies, and innovative enterprises), as well as departmental collaboration, hierarchical relationships, and cultural construction within the enterprise. Environmental dimension: Studies the interaction between enterprises and the external environment, such as market competition, policies and regulations, technological changes (such as digital transformation), and their impacts on management models.
